description: Localized battle/cutscene subtitle lines, keyed by a text id usually derived from the voice id; consumed through the shared GameText subsystem when a level-sequence subtitle widget is opened.

ID.simple: Text id / row key used to request the subtitle.
ID.technical: FName declared in FGameDataTableRow_GameText and serialized alongside the UDataTable row name; the loader keys every language variant as BattleSubTitleTextDataTable_<EApplicationLanguage name>. Lookup uses this value as the FName passed to UDataTable::FindRow across the ordered 14-table GameText array. For battle subtitles the id is normally the Voice row id with its first two characters removed (voice id 'VS...'/'Btl...' style), and HasText gates whether the subtitle widget opens. Casing is preserved in FNames but FindRow resolves by FName equality.

Text.simple: The localized subtitle string displayed on screen.
Text.technical: FString (row +0x10 in the retail layout); returned by value. Missing rows return an empty FString. Before display it passes through FormatText: <TYPE=KEY>[MODS] tags are regex-matched and replaced (GLO from the glossary map, DYN from request parameters; modifiers ABS/RATE_TO_PCT/FULL_WIDTH/HALF_WIDTH/DECIMAL_PLACE_1..4). Embedded newlines are collapsed to nothing for Ja/Zh_Hant/Zh_Hans and to a space for other languages when a text block has bForceOneLine. This group's exported rows contain no tags in the En export, but the shared formatter still applies.

notes: Row struct is FGameDataTableRow_GameText (ID, Text) for all 11 exported language variants; all variants share the same 1131 row ids in the companion export. The table base name is hard-coded in AGameTextManager::StartLanguageLoading and in Tick; the suffix is the EApplicationLanguage enum name, and Config/DefaultGame.ini:35-45 assigns the 11 language variants to separate cooked chunks.

Two call paths use these ids: AGameSequencerManager derives a subtitle id from a playing voice row (right-side substring after the first two characters) and opens the StoryDemoSubtitle part; UAbramsSequencerSoundModule::ShowSubtitle accepts an explicit id and either opens that part or queues a request. Both first call HasText, so only ids actually present in one of the loaded GameText tables produce a visible subtitle. The subtitle widget itself sets a text id, which the normal text block resolves through GetText.
Subtitle visibility is also gated by the user setting Settings.bSubtitlesEnabled when the level-sequence part is opened (GameLevelSequenceWidget.cpp:29-30).

Ordering matters for id collisions: FindTextRow walks the 14 tables in the fixed order listed in GameTextManager.cpp:548-564 and returns the first row found; BattleSubTitleTextDataTable_<Lang> is slot 11. No code dispatches by prefix, so a colliding non-SYS_ id in an earlier table wins.

Reconstruction caveat: GetGameText/GetSystemText/FormatText are byte-matched to retail; FindTextRow and AGameTextManager::Tick are behaviour-certified rather than byte-identical (status/functions.json rows 0x14af290, 0x14af3d0, 0x14c96f0; BEHAV record BG03). Member and helper names are reconstructed, and only a partial Content set is available, so no claim is made about retail Blueprint-only consumers or assets outside the exports.

usages.detail: Builds SubtitleId from the playing voice row id, tests HasText, opens the level-sequence subtitle part and sets that id on the widget.
ShowSubtitle(TextId) checks HasText, then either opens the subtitle widget or queues UGameWidgetManager::RequestSubtitle with the same id.
SetSubtitleTextId stores the id on the embedded subtitle text block; ClosePart on the voice player event removes the subtitle.
Installs the localized BattleSubTitleTextDataTable_<Language> into the shared TextDataTables array used by all non-SYS_ text requests.
A text block's SetTextRequest resolves any text id (including subtitle ids) through AGameTextManager::GetText and caches the resulting string.
